memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses also took the breast, which was his share of the ordination ram, and waved it before the LORD as a wave offering, as the LORD commanded Moses." - Lev 8:29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses receives a portion. And then he waves it before the LORD too.

He does not simply pocket it. Even his own rightful share is lifted up to God before he takes it.

There is real integrity in that. Moses was the one conducting the ceremony. Nobody would have questioned him. He could have taken his portion quietly and no one would have thought twice.

Instead, he did publicly with his own share exactly what he had just required of Aaron.

Leaders who exempt themselves from what they ask of others do enormous damage. Jesus said of the religious leaders of his day, They tie up heavy, cumbersome loads and put them on other people's shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to lift a finger to move them (Mtt 23:4).

Paul could say the opposite: Follow my example, as I follow the example of Christ (1 Cor 11:1). Peter told elders to be examples to the flock (1 Pet 5:3).

There is also a poignant note here. Moses conducted this whole ceremony and did not become the priest. He installed his brother into a role he would never hold, and went back to his own work without complaint.

Faithfulness sometimes means preparing someone else for a place you will never occupy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I hold myself to the standards I expect from others?
2. Can I serve gladly in preparing someone else for a role I will never have?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from asking of others what I will not do myself. Give me joy in serving Your purposes even when the honour goes elsewhere. Amen.
